body: The White House is urging Congress to approve an additional $30.1 billion for US aviation infrastructure upgrades. Reuters reports that Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy and budget director Russell Vought are pushing for action before Democrats take control of Congress in January. In a November 13 letter to congressional leaders, Duffy and Vought requested swift approval of the investment, saying: "This investment is critical to complete the modernization of our national airspace." With Democrats preparing to assume control of Congress on January 3, 2027, the administration is seeking to advance the proposal during the remaining weeks of Republican control, although the legislation's prospects remain uncertain.

The proposed funding breaks down into $10.1 billion for air traffic control modernization, automation and cloud computing, $2.0 billion to replace and improve air traffic control towers, and $18.0 billion for airport infrastructure, including $10 billion to modernize or replace aging terminals. Together with the $12.5 billion approved in 2025, federal aviation modernization funding would reach approximately $42.6 billion. The administration argues the funding is essential to replacing outdated air traffic control equipment, improving airport capacity and strengthening the safety of the national airspace system. The modernization program was announced in 2025 after years of concern about aging communications infrastructure, controller shortages and operational disruptions. According to Duffy, 68% of the FAA's legacy copper telecommunications network has already been replaced with high-speed fiber infrastructure.

The appeal is a renewed effort rather than an entirely new funding initiative. Duffy first called for approximately $30 billion in additional funding on September 22, shortly after a major Northeast air traffic control disruption, and Senator Eric Schmitt introduced the Modern Skies Act on September 28, supported by major airlines and aviation industry organizations. The funding appeal coincided with a nationwide ground stop ordered by the FAA on November 13, citing extraordinary circumstances and safety reasons, with international arrivals handled individually; according to Axios, the cause had not been officially established at the time of writing. The September incident demonstrated how communications failures can spread disruption: a circuit failed at an air traffic facility in Philadelphia, while an Amtrak construction crew accidentally severed a fiber-optic cable in New Jersey, and ground stops affected Newark, Philadelphia and New York's airports, with knock-on delays extending to Boston.
en.summary: The White House is urging Congress to approve an additional $30.1 billion for US aviation infrastructure upgrades, with Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy and budget director Russell Vought pressing for action before Democrats take control of Congress in January 2027.
en.title: White House urges Congress to approve $30.1 billion for US aviation infrastructure and air traffic upgrades

body: 白宮正敦促國會批准額外301億美元美國航空基礎設施升級經費。據路透社報導，運輸部長達菲（Sean Duffy）與預算主任沃特（Russell Vought）正推動在民主黨明年1月接掌國會前完成立法。兩人11月13日致函國會領袖，要求迅速批准這筆投資；民主黨預定2027年1月3日接掌國會，政府希望在共和黨掌控國會的最後幾週內推進提案，不過法案前景仍不明朗，國會領導層更替也不必然意味經費會遭否決。

這筆經費的用途已有明確分配：航管現代化、自動化與雲端運算101億美元，航管塔台汰換與改善20億美元，機場基礎設施180億美元，其中100億美元用於航廈現代化或汰換。若加上2025年已批准的125億美元，聯邦航空現代化經費總額將達約426億美元。政府表示，這筆經費對汰換老舊航管設備、提升機場容量、強化國家空域系統安全至關重要；相關現代化計畫2025年公布，起因於外界多年來對老化通訊基礎設施、管制員短缺與營運中斷的憂慮。據達菲表示，FAA傳統銅纜電信網路已有68%汰換為高速光纖基礎設施。

這次呼籲並非全新的經費倡議，而是先前提案的延續。達菲9月22日已在美國東北部航管大停擺後要求追加約300億美元，參議員施密特（Eric Schmitt）9月28日提出《現代天空法案》，獲主要航空公司與業界組織支持。同一天，FAA也曾因特殊情況與安全考量下令全美地面停飛，要求離港航班原地待命，國際入境航班則個案處理；據Axios報導，發布時停飛原因尚未正式確認。這次停飛之前，9月東北部航管系統曾因費城航管設施電路故障與Amtrak施工隊在新澤西州切斷光纖纜線而大規模中斷，紐華克、費城與紐約各機場實施地面停飛，延誤擴及波士頓。
zh.summary: 白宮敦促國會批准額外301億美元美國航空基建經費，運輸部長達菲與預算主任沃特11月13日致函國會領袖，盼在民主黨明年1月接掌國會前完成立法。
